title: Starting the process
content:
## What can be built?

Emergent's mobile build system supports three types of mobile applications:

- **Native Android apps** — compiled APKs that install on Android devices and publish to Google Play Console.
- **Native iOS apps** — compiled IPA files that install on iPhones and publish to the App Store.
- **Progressive Web Apps (PWAs)** — installable web apps that run in a browser but feel native, with offline support and home-screen shortcuts.

<Note title="Platform support note">
Apple Watch and iPad apps can be coded (Swift/SwiftUI) within Emergent but cannot yet be published to the App Store through the platform. Support for these platforms is coming soon.
</Note>

All mobile apps are built using **React Native** and the **Expo framework**, which share a single codebase for both iOS and Android.

---

## Requirements

Before you start building, make sure you have:

<Steps>
<Step title="An Emergent account">
Sign up or log in at [emergent.build](https://emergent.build). You'll use the **Mobile Agent** from within your workspace.
</Step>

<Step title="The Expo Go app (for testing)">
Download **Expo Go** on your phone—it's free on both the App Store (iOS) and Google Play (Android). You'll use it to scan a QR code and preview your app live without publishing.
</Step>

<Step title="Developer accounts (for publishing)">
To ship to production, you need:

- **Apple Developer Program** account ($99/year) for iOS.
- **Google Play Console** account (one-time $25 fee) for Android.

<Warning>
Apple account approval takes **24–48 hours**. Create your account early in the process to avoid delays when you're ready to publish.
</Warning>
</Step>
</Steps>

For more on the publishing step, see [Publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores).

---

## What is Expo?

**Expo** is the open-source framework and toolchain that powers every mobile app you build in Emergent. It sits on top of React Native and provides:

- A managed build service (no Xcode or Android Studio required on your machine).
- Over-the-air updates—push fixes without resubmitting to the stores.
- A comprehensive library of native modules (camera, location, notifications, etc.).

**Expo Go** is a free companion app for iOS and Android. During development, you scan a QR code from the Emergent workspace and your app runs **live on your device**—no need to compile an APK, no App Store submission, no waiting. Code changes appear instantly.

<Tip>
Think of Expo Go as a live sandbox: it's perfect for prototyping, iteration, and demos. When you're ready to ship, Emergent builds a standalone binary you submit to the stores.
</Tip>

---

## Development workflow

Building a mobile app in Emergent follows a tight feedback loop between you and the Mobile Agent:

<Steps>
<Step title="Open the Mobile Agent and describe your app">
Navigate to the **Build › Mobile Apps** section of your workspace. Start a new conversation with the Mobile Agent and describe what you want to build—features, screens, data, design preferences, integrations.
</Step>

<Step title="Answer clarifying questions">
The agent will ask follow-up questions about authentication, navigation style, API endpoints, branding, and any ambiguities in your request. Answer these in the chat to refine the spec.
</Step>

<Step title="Preview live on your phone via Expo Go">
Once the agent generates the app, it displays a **QR code** in the workspace. Open Expo Go on your phone, tap **Scan QR code**, and point your camera at the screen. Your app launches immediately.

<Info>
Both your computer and phone must be on the same Wi-Fi network for the preview to work. If you see a connection error, check your network or use the tunnel option (available in advanced settings).
</Info>
</Step>

<Step title="Iterate and debug with the agent">
Test the app on your device. If something is broken or missing, describe the issue in the chat. The agent will update the code, and the preview reloads automatically. Repeat until you're satisfied.
</Step>

<Step title="Move to publishing when ready">
When the app is stable and feature-complete, proceed to [Publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores) to create production builds and submit them to Google Play and the App Store.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Converting an existing web app?">
If you've already built a web app in Emergent and want a mobile version, see [Web ↔ Mobile conversion](/web-mobile-conversion-canonical) for guidance on adapting layouts, navigation, and state.
</Tip>

For a step-by-step walkthrough of your first build, see [Your first build (walkthrough)](/your-first-build-walkthrough). For an overview of how Emergent turns chat into deployed apps, read [The chat-to-deployment flow](/the-chat-to-deployment-flow).
